profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point, tagged telecom=data_center, is named "Factory Software | AVEVA Select Italia." AVEVA is a real, publicly traded industrial software company, listed on the London Stock Exchange, that provides engineering design, operations management, and asset-performance software used across manufacturing, energy, and process industries worldwide. "AVEVA Select" is the branding AVEVA uses for its network of regional reseller and systems-integrator partners, and this record most plausibly identifies an Italian partner office selling and supporting AVEVA's software products under that program, likely operating under the name "Factory Software" as the local reseller entity. A software reseller and integrator's office maintains its own business IT systems but is not a data-center operator; the telecom=data_center tag here is best read as a mistag of the office's own server or IT closet.

reading.body:
This record is a software reseller's office in Italy, not a data center, misidentified by an OpenStreetMap tagging error.

Factory Software operates as a regional partner office for AVEVA, a London-listed industrial software company that sells engineering and operations-management tools to manufacturing and process industries. The office maintains its own IT systems, likely including a server closet or small internal network infrastructure, which someone tagged in OpenStreetMap as a data center. This misclassification conflates a business IT installation with a facility designed to house compute infrastructure at scale.

The distinction matters because AI infrastructure mapping depends on accurate location data. Confusing software reseller offices with data centers creates false positives in any geographic inventory of computing facilities. This entry should be excluded from analyses of actual compute capacity or power demand, since an office's internal IT closet does not contribute meaningfully to either metric.

The data does not reveal whether Factory Software's office has any involvement in deploying or supporting AI applications for its customers. It only confirms the facility is a software business presence, not a power-consuming computing hub.
